lines.en: : ...and that’s how you find slope-intercept form. Any questions?
: Umm...could you please repeat...all of that?
: Sensei, I have no idea what else I’m supposed to do. She’s just not retaining any information.
: That’s just because you keep using big words and weird terms like ‘slope intercept form.’ Who the heck even knows what that is?!
: Everyone! Or at least we’re supposed to!
: Ahhhh! Why can’t all of our tests just be about how to be a good caretaker?!
: If you can’t even figure out slope intercept form, there’s no way you’re a good caretaker.
: Those two things have absolutely nothing in common!
: And besides, I’m a much better caretaker than you’ll ever be, Makoto!
: Take that back!
: No!
: Yes!
: No!
So-
I bet you’re probably wondering how I ended up in this position.
And, to be honest, I am too.
It all started with Ami coming up to me in class and asking for help with algebra.
Of course, Ami wanted me around as well, so...
Here we are. ‘Learning’ things.
: You two really don’t get along, do you?
: Makoto is just jealous because you spend more time with me than her.
: I-I am not! I’m just trying to help you so you don’t get held back!
: See? She’s yelling at me to try and impress you but you’re not impressed at all, are you Sensei?
: I’m...wait...what’s going on, exactly?
: Sensei! Tell her to focus or she’s never going to get into a good[school] and become a doctor.
: I don’t wanna be a doctor! I wanna be a housewife!
: Who in their right mind would marry someone who doesn’t even know slope intercept form?!
: None of your business!
: I bet Sensei doesn’t even know the formula for that!
Please don’t drag me into this.
: Preposterous! Of course he does!
: No way! He doesn’t like boring stuff like that!
: It’s not boring just because it’s educational!
: Sensei! What is the formula for slope intercept form?!
: Uhh...
m = bx + y
: Definitely ‘m = bx + y.’
: Tch-!
: Teehee~ Told you he doesn’t know!
: Sensei isn’t interested in that kind of stuff!
: That’s simply not true! Of course he’s interested in that kind of stuff. He just had...a momentary memory lapse.
: Things like that happen.
: Whatever you say, Makoto~
y = mx + b
: Easy. ‘y = mx + b.’
: Ah-!
: I expected nothing less from you, Sensei.
: Why do you know the answer to that?!
: Hey, I might not be the best at showing it...or applying it...but I’m actually pretty smart.
: I’m offended you’d think otherwise, Ami.
: If it’s any consolation, I’ve never judged you at all. I think you’re brilliant and wonderful and the best man I’ve ever met.
: Who are you calling a smartypants glasses-wearer?!
: The one who is a smartypants and is also wearing glasses!
x = by + m
: Definitely ‘x = by + m.’
: Tch-!
: Teehee~ Told you he doesn’t know!
: Sensei isn’t interested in that kind of stuff!
: That’s simply not true! Of course he’s interested in that kind of stuff. He just had...a momentary memory lapse.
: Things like that happen.
: Whatever you say, Makoto~
: Listen, you two. It doesn’t matter whether or not I know this formula. What matters is that both of you do.
: I’d hate to see something as simple as this hold either of you back.
And I’d also hate to get in trouble for having some of my students fail the standardized test.
Thank god that Makoto is able to tutor everyone on things that I can’t remember or never learned in the first place.
: Well said, Sensei.
: I mean, obviously you don’t have to worry about me. But those words are very wise when applied to everyone else.
: Can't you just study with me instead, Sensei? Makoto is a mean teacher.
: I’m sorry, Ami...I just get frustrated whenever it seems like someone isn’t paying attention.
: So...you’re not gonna be a big meanie anymore?
: I...will do my best to not be a ‘big meanie...’
: ...Fine. I guess I can try a little harder, too.
: So, can we finally move on with things?
: Can you do one more thing for me, first?
: Of course. What do you need?
: Can you admit that Sensei likes cute girls like me more than he likes nerdy ones like you?
: Hey, don’t look at me. I can’t control her.
: She’s your [niece]. Can’t you at least tell her to focus?
: Uhh...I can try?
: Ami, focus.
: Yes, Sensei!~
: Hah...how about we just take a break instead?
: That works for me! I was getting tired of all the slopey stuff anyway.
: It’s slope int- ahh, forget it. Let’s just talk about something the two of us have in common instead.
: Sure! Did you have anything in mind? The two of us have never really talked about stuff we have in common before.
: That’s true. I don’t think I know much about you at all, Ami.
: How about you tell me your top three interests and I’ll see if any of mine match up?
: Hmm...my top three interests...Okay. So, in no particular order-
: Cats, rabbits, and Sensei.
: Your...[uncle] is in your top three interests?
: Of course. I love him and he loves me.
: Isn’t that a little...uhh...
: Hm? A little what?
: ...Nothing.
: What are your top three, Makoto? Do we have any of the same stuff?
: Uhhh...well it’s kind of embarrassing to say this in front of him, but...
: I guess Sensei would be in my top three interests as well.
: Of course, it’s just because of how much of a role model he’s been for me in terms of teaching and...
: Umm...yeah.
: So...I guess we could talk about that if you want.
: Ami?
: I’m keeping an eye on you, Makoto...
: What? Did I...do something wrong?...
In the end, Ami never learned how slope intercept form works.
She wound up memorizing the formula, though, so hopefully she can just...figure it out come test-day.
As for the relationship between these two-
Well...I’m starting to think it’s just destined to not ever work out...
